subject: Greenfield Labs — MSA/Order Form redlines and DPA/SCCs role allocation
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@greenfieldlabs.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenfieldlabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (DPA/SCCs queries)

Hi David,

Thanks again for the call this morning. I've attached the redline (Greenfield_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a quick DPA/SCCs matrix (DPA_SCCs_matrix.xlsx) showing our asks. High-level items we need your help with:

- Confirm role split: Greenfield expects to be Controller for customer data; they want Redwood to acknowledge Processor obligations and confirm subcontractor/subprocessor flowdown (specifically for the analytics subprocessor).
- SCCs: we need confirmation on which SCC version Redwood will sign (2021 SCCs vs amended template).
- Transfer impact addendum: we have a clause asking for a transfer addendum if any processing leaves the EEA — can Redwood provide a fallback (e.g., EU exit plan or onshore-only routing for EU customers)?
- KMS/HSM and evidence: our security team requests KMS coverage for encryption keys and a note on audit log retention windows for compliance reviews.

We are targeting a procurement signature by Dec 10. Can you confirm ownership on your side for the DPA redline and whether legal needs anything else from our counsel (Josh Park, cc'd on separate thread)?

I attached the files and left inline comments in the redline.

Thanks,
Sara Lewis
Legal Ops Manager
Greenfield Labs

Attachments: Greenfield_MSA_redline_v3.docx (comments), DPA_SCCs_matrix.xlsx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@greenfieldlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (DPA/SCCs queries)

Sara — thanks for the clear notes and the files. Looping in Laura (counsel) for legal redline response and Ben for procurement/timing.

Short answers up front:
- Role split: Redwood accepts Processor role in contract language; we'll add explicit subcontractor flowdown obligations and will provide the current subprocessor list as an attachment or link.
- SCCs: Redwood's standard is the 2021 EU SCCs (controller-processor modules where applicable). We are open to the amended template but need to run a quick internal check against hosting regions.
- Transfer addendum: we can offer an EU-only routing commitment for core customer data for a defined period (e.g., during the pilot/first 12 months) or a documented fallback if routing outside EEA is required.
- KMS/Audit logs: we can confirm KMS integration options (bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM for private deployments) and provide retention audit evidence for a standard 12-month window; longer retention can be discussed as a commercial add-on.

Laura — can you take the attached redline and propose language for: (1) Processor acknowledgement + subprocessor flowdown; (2) SCC selection language and a short paragraph for a transfer impact addendum fallback; (3) a KMS/Audit notes clause (we should be precise on what we can commit to for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments).

Ben — can you confirm if Greenfield is ok with the EU-only routing commitment vs pricing impact if they require strict residency? They mentioned a pricing/ops decision maker that may need to sign off.

Thanks — I'll coordinate the DocuSign timeline once we have redline agreement.

Best,
David Kim
Contracts Lead, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@greenfieldlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:21:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (DPA/SCCs queries)

Hi all,

I've reviewed the redline and the DPA matrix. High-level proposed edits below (I'll produce a tracked version by EOD Nov 29).

1) Roles and flowdown
- Proposed clause: "Redwood Inference acknowledges that, with respect to Customer Personal Data processed under the Agreement, Customer is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. Redwood shall ensure that its subprocessors are subject to written contractual commitments consistent with the obligations of this DPA and the applicable SCCs."
- Add: a short schedule listing current subprocessors and a 30-day notice/objection window for new subprocessors.

2) SCCs selection
- Proposed: incorporate 2021 SCCs (controller-processor module) by reference as Annex X; include a statement that the parties shall execute the then-current EU Commission SCCs applicable to controller-processor relationships.
- If Greenfield insists on amended templates, we'll accept but require a limited review period for hosting compatibility and an explicit fallback if incompatibilities are discovered.

3) Transfer impact addendum / routing commitment
- Options to offer: (A) EU-only routing for processing of Customer Personal Data for an initial 12-month period (no additional fee); (B) Permanent EU residency for an additional fee and delivery timeline TBD; (C) Fallback: approved documented transfer addendum (scope-limited) that requires customer sign-off for any EEA->non-EEA processing beyond the routing commitment.
- Language will include an SLA for notifying Customer 45 days before any change that would materially affect routing.

4) KMS / audit logs / evidence
- For hosted Redwood: we can offer customer-specific KMS via our dedicated offering (Bring-Your-Own-Key for Dedicated and Private deployments only). Hosted customers receive encryption-at-rest with provider-managed keys; we can provide SOC2-type attestations and 12 months of audit log retention by default.
- Proposed clause: define what counts as "audit evidence" and provide a timetable for evidentiary delivery (e.g., security questionnaire + screenshots within 5 business days; export of relevant logs within 15 business days under NDA).

5) Next steps / timeline
- I'll send tracked edits (MSA + DPA) by EOD Nov 29. David / Ben, please confirm if procurement can accept the 12-month EU routing trial or whether Greenfield needs permanent residency priced up front.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: will send tracked redline (MSA + DPA)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@greenfieldlabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:09:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (DPA/SCCs queries)

Quick commercial note from procurement side: Greenfield indicated via procurement that they're fine with the 12-month EU routing trial as long as the fallback/procurement path to permanent residency is clearly priced and time-boxed (we should provide a ballpark: +20-30% uplift on Order Form for a permanent EU-only tenant and estimated lead time 6-9 weeks).

If Laura's legal edits keep the 12-month trial as "no additional fee" and the permanent residency option as a priced add-on, procurement should be able to proceed toward signature by Dec 10.

I'll prepare a short pricing addendum draft and share with Laura for reference.

— Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Josh Park <josh@slawfirm.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@greenfieldlabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:48:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (DPA/SCCs queries)

Laura / David — thanks for the proposed approach. A few clarifying points from external counsel for Greenfield (quick read):

- SCCs: confirming acceptance of the 2021 SCCs is fine. Please ensure the Annex references the correct module (controller -> processor).
- KMS: Greenfield will need written confirmation that for Dedicated/Private deployments we support BYOK KMS (and the mechanism for key rotation). For hosted, they accept provider-managed keys but will require contractual confirmation of key-handling procedures and access restrictions.
- Audit evidence: the 12-month retention is acceptable; however, we need a commitment that exportable audit logs covering data access and admin actions will be available within the 15-business-day window under NDA. Please capture that as a contractual right to obtain evidence for lawful audits.
- Transfer addendum / fallback: Greenfield asks that the fallback include a concrete escalation path (named point of contact in Redwood Legal/Operations) and a remediation timeline (30 days for mitigation steps; 90 days for a permanent residency migration plan).

I forwarded the client's inline comments separately; Laura, if you could incorporate the access-to-evidence and escalation path language into the tracked DPA, I think procurement can clear this.

Best,
Josh Park
Partner, S/Law LLP
